Subject: Recap: Deployment-mode discussion (shared vs dedicated) & next steps

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary drivers: predictable latency for peak billing flows, isolation from other tenants for PCI-scope requests, and predictable unit economics.
- Current target: support ~100 RPS peak for auth/charge endpoints, with p99 latency target under 500ms (for text-generation API calls).
- Data residency: production data must reside in our US region; potential interest in a VPC/private deployment later for audit reasons.

Deployment options discussed
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, lower unit cost, but multi-tenant (best-effort isolation).
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with stronger isolation (dedicated nodes/GPU pools), configurable autoscaling, SLA-backed targets possible via Dedicated contract.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network and control plane, for maximum isolation and compliance.

Primary concerns you raised
- Noisy-neighbor effects during platform-level peaks
- Clear isolation boundaries between FinPay traffic and other tenants
- SLOs/SLA for p99 latency and error budgets

Proposed next steps
1) Priyom to follow up with a short tech note on noisy-neighbor mitigations and isolation boundaries (we'll include kernel/quantization notes where relevant).
2) Share a short SLO/SLA summary and an initial mutual action plan — attaching both in this email.
3) Schedule a 60-minute architecture workshop next week to validate capacity numbers and pilot approach.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, redwood-slos-summary.pdf

If this looks right, Alice — can you confirm the p99/throughput numbers and preferred times for a workshop next week?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Confirming numbers: yes, our immediate target is ~100 RPS for peak payment flows. For the tokenization/generation endpoints we need p99 under 500ms and p50 under 120ms. We are willing to accept a small error budget but need clear SLO reporting.

2) Noisy neighbor: our compliance team is particularly concerned with tail latency introduced by co-tenants during model warmups/large-batch training traffic. We need to understand isolation guarantees (logical vs physical), and what guarantees Redwood can offer for dedicated pools.

3) Data residency / compliance: production must remain in our US region. For PCI/regulated components we may require a VPC/private deployment if Dedicated cannot meet audit requirements.

4) Procurement timeline: we have a Q2 procurement window and need a ballpark on time to pilot + PoC (targeting 4–6 week pilot if possible).

Attaching our internal requirements doc (finpay-requirements.pdf) — it includes baseline traffic patterns and compliance notes.

Can Priyom and Marissa propose a short scope for the workshop and a very rough cost band for a Dedicated pilot so procurement has a number to evaluate?

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform Engineering
FinPay

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the detail. Quick technical answers and a proposed pilot approach below.

Isolation & noisy-neighbor mitigations (Dedicated)
- Physical isolation: Dedicated capacity provisions customer-dedicated GPU instances (no co-located tenant processes on the same GPU). That removes most noisy-neighbor sources tied to GPU contention.
- Logical isolation (Shared): our Shared hosted tier uses strong scheduling, request prioritization, and continuous batching; we maintain per-tenant prefix cache boundaries and offer soft isolation but cannot guarantee physical GPU exclusivity.
- KV/prefix cache isolation: in Dedicated we can allocate dedicated cache memory per customer and pin model shards to dedicated nodes to avoid cross-tenant eviction.
- Autoscaling: Dedicated supports reserved baseline capacity + burst policies. Burst is subject to regional capacity but will not colocate other tenants on reserved nodes.

SLOs and SLAs
- For Dedicated customers we provide SLA-backed availability and latency targets in the contract. For example, we can commit to a p99 latency SLO (measured on our side) with defined credits for breaches. We'll need to lock down model size, sequence length profile, and concurrency targets to write a precise SLO.

Pilot proposal (4–6 weeks)
1) Architecture workshop (60–90m): review traffic profiles, models, sequence lengths; define success criteria and SLO measurement. (Week 1)
2) Provision Dedicated pilot pool sized for 100 RPS target with room for 20% headroom. We'll run a test harness with synthetic traffic and your sample payloads to validate p99/p50. (Weeks 2–3)
3) Observability run & tuning: tune batching/kv cache/quantization settings to hit latency targets and capture traces/metrics for your compliance team. (Week 4)
4) Post-pilot findings + procurement packet: SLO report, config recommendations, and proposed billing/commit options. (Week 5)

Estimated cost band (very rough, ballpark)
- Dedicated pilot (4–6 weeks): includes reserved GPU capacity + engineering support — estimated $25k–$45k depending on GPU instance family and required replication for HA. We will provide a formal quote once we finalize pool size and replication needs.

Attachments: redwood-arch-dedicated.pdf, redwood-slos-summary.pdf

If that looks reasonable I can work with Marissa to schedule the workshop (we have availability next Tue/Wed morning PT).

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
